Extract predicted components from a Random Planted Forest

Source: R/predict_components.R, R/prune.R
predict_components.Rd

Prediction components are a functional decomposition of the model prediction. The sum of all components equals the overall predicted value for an observation.

Usage

predict_components(object, new_data, ...)

# S3 method for class 'rpf'
predict_components(
  object,
  new_data,
  max_interaction = NULL,
  predictors = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'rpf_pruned'
predict_components(
  object,
  new_data,
  max_interaction = NULL,
  predictors = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

[rpf | rpf_pruned]: A fitted rpf model, or a pruned one from prune_components() or rpf().

new_data

[data.frame | matrix]: New observations to predict.

...

Not currently used, but required for extensibility. Unknown arguments are an error.

max_interaction

[integer(1) | NULL: NULL]: Maximum degree of interactions to consider. NULL uses the max_interaction parameter from the rpf object. Must be between 1 (main effects only) and the max_interaction of the rpf object.

predictors

[character | NULL: NULL]: Vector of one or more names of the forest's predictors to extract components for. These are the columns the forest was fitted on: with a formula, its terms, such as log(x1). If NULL, all predictors and their interactions are returned, in the order of the fit's columns.

Value

A list with elements:

  • m (data.table): Components for each main effect and interaction term, representing the functional decomposition of the prediction. All components together with the intercept sum up to the prediction. For multiclass classification, the number of output columns is multiplied by the number of target_levels: the levels of the outcome, or for loss = "logit" all levels but the first (the reference level).

  • intercept (numeric): Expected value of the prediction. For multiclass classification, one value per target level, named by target_levels.

  • x (data.table): The predictors selected by predictors, as the forest sees them in new_data (with a formula, its terms, such as log(x1)).

  • target_levels (character): For multiclass classification only: Vector of target levels which can be used to disassemble m, as names include both term and target level.

  • remainder (numeric): Only if m leaves out components of the forest: if predictors leaves out some of the forest's predictors, if max_interaction (lowered to the number of predictors) is below that of the rpf object, or if the forest was purified with a maxp_interaction below it (see purify()). The prediction minus intercept and m's row sums, so that the three sum to the prediction. For multiclass classification, one column per target level.

Details

Extracts all possible components up to max_interaction degrees, up to the value set when calling rpf(). The intercept is always included. Optionally predictors can be specified to only include components made of the given predictors; the sum of the other components is returned as remainder. If max_interaction is greater than length(predictors), the max_interaction will be lowered accordingly.

All components are evaluated in one pass over the rows of new_data. Components that the purified forest does not hold, such as sets of predictors that never appear together in a tree, are zero columns.

The components are only unique for a purified forest; purify() says how they are identified. An unpurified forest is purified in place on first use with the defaults of purify(). For other settings, such as more threads, call purify() before predict_components().

Note

Depending on the number of predictors and max_interaction, the number of components will increase drastically to sum(choose(ncol(new_data), seq_len(max_interaction))).

Pruned forests

For an rpf_pruned object from prune_components() or rpf(), m holds only the kept components, each scaled by its coefficient beta_S, and intercept is the pruned model's intercept alpha, so that they sum to predict() of the pruned model. Components that are not kept are absent, not zero columns. If predictors or max_interaction leave out kept components, their sum is returned as remainder.

Examples


# Regression task, only some predictors
train <-  mtcars[1:20, 1:4]
test <-  mtcars[21:32, 1:4]

set.seed(23)
rpfit <- rpf(mpg ~ ., data = train, max_interaction = 3, ntrees = 30)

# Extract all components, including main effects and interaction terms up to `max_interaction`
(components <- predict_components(rpfit, test))

# sums to prediction
cbind(
  m_sum = rowSums(components$m) + components$intercept,
  prediction = predict(rpfit, test)
)
